body.target_estimand: \(\tau_P(0)\), defined exclusively as the value at zero of the unique continuous extension of \(\mu_{1,P}-\mu_{0,P}\)
body.estimand_functional:
The causal target is \(\tau_P(0)\), already identified from the observed law by \(\mathrm{prop:causal\mbox{-}identification}\).  The supplied-propensity attainer in \(\mathrm{thm:oracle\mbox{-}minimax}\) is the following explicit total map.  Let \(D=[1/2,1]^d\), let \(v_\gamma(z)\) be the vector of all monomials \(z^\nu\) of total degree at most \(\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\), and define the deterministic positive-definite matrix and polynomial kernel
\[
 H_\gamma=\int_D v_\gamma(z)v_\gamma(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz,
 \qquad
 q_\gamma(z)=v_\gamma(0)^{\mathsf T}H_\gamma^{-1}v_\gamma(z).
\]
Set \(h_n=n^{-1/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\).  For each observation with \(X_i\in h_nD\), compute
\[
 Z_i^e=\frac{A_iY_i}{e_P(X_i)}-\frac{(1-A_i)Y_i}{1-e_P(X_i)},
\]
and set its summand to zero when \(X_i\notin h_nD\).  With \(\Pi_{[-3/4,3/4]}(u)=\min\{\max\{u,-3/4\},3/4\}\), output
\[
 \widehat\tau_n^e(0)=\Pi_{[-3/4,3/4]}\!\left(
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n h_n^{-d}q_\gamma(X_i/h_n)
 \mathbf 1\{X_i\in h_nD\}Z_i^e
 \right).
\]
The monomial basis, exact Gram integral and inverse, bandwidth, finite average, and clipping are deterministic finite operations.  Since \(h_nD\) is separated from the propensity-zero corner and \(e_P\) is bounded away from zero on that annulus, no displayed denominator vanishes; setting the summand to zero off the annulus makes the estimator total on every dataset.  It attains \(R_n^e\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\) for every \(\kappa\geq0\).

For \(\kappa=0\), the established data-only functional is the total second-order estimator \(\widehat\tau^{(2)}_{n,h,k}(0)\) constructed in \(\mathrm{lem:bounded\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}risk}\).  It uses a one-sided localized polynomial fit, a finite projection correction with the known exact Lebesgue Gram matrix, deterministic rank rounding, singular-value flooring, clipping, and an all-dataset fallback.  With \(S=\alpha+\beta\), \(S_\star=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2S)\), deterministic tuning gives
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}
 \leq R_n(d,0,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C\max\left\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\right\}.
\]
This is an explicitly total exact-uniform specialization of the bounded-overlap higher-order architecture: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE already covers the same upper rate and elbow and applies when the design is known uniform.  The data-only and supplied-propensity risks have the same pure-power rate when \(S\geq S_\star\), including equality without a logarithmic factor.  Below that elbow the displayed upper bound is proved but its matching exact-uniform nuisance lower bound is not.

For \(\kappa>0\), the total first-order functional from \(\mathrm{thm:first\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}upper}\) gives, with \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\),
\[
 c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}
 \leq R_n(d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)
 \leq C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)},
\]
and the unresolved higher-order local-zero branches are precisely those retained in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}frontier}\).

sampling_model.design: Known exactly uniform random design on \([0,1]^d\) with \(n\) independent observations.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is strictly positive almost everywhere and equals zero only at \(x=0\) when \(\kappa>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) and the uniform design law, but not \(g_P\), \(e_P\), \(\mu_{0,P}\), or \(\tau_P\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 already give the same bounded-overlap higher-order upper rate and nuisance elbow and apply when the design is known uniform; the displayed lower construction in Definition 1 uses a covariate density supported on a perforated set.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: An explicitly total one-sided exact-uniform specialization using the known Lebesgue Gram matrix, deterministic rank rounding, singular-value flooring, clipping, and an all-dataset fallback; no new bounded-overlap rate or elbow is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 bounds a local-polynomial R-learner under bounded estimated propensities and nondegenerate local Gram matrices.
Theorem 2.1 controls the affinity between two convex mixtures when perturbations localize to a measurable partition.
The random-design variance-functional results use local-polynomial U-statistics and a fuzzy lower construction to expose a regression-functional elbow.
Theorem 1 analyzes empirical-Gram higher-order influence-function corrections that remove a covariate-density smoothness requirement for average doubly robust functionals.
Theorem 2 gives near-minimax integrated \(L_1\) rates for random treated and control designs under bounded density ratios and contrast smoothness at most one.
Theorem 1 gives the scalar pointwise regression rate under a regularly varying design density through a local-mass balance.
The weak-overlap results derive thresholded average-effect limit laws and a scalar regression smoothness degradation under propensity-tail restrictions.
Corollary 4 gives pointwise RKHS CATE rates without consistent propensity estimation while retaining a uniform positive overlap parameter.

body.tldr: For the exact local-zero model, the sharp supplied-propensity theorem gives \(R_n^e\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\) for every \(\kappa\geq0\) by an explicit annular estimator and genuine full-support exact-uniform Bernoulli lower laws.  The total data-only first-order estimator gives \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\leq R_n\leq C n^{-t/(2t+d+\kappa)}\), where \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\).  At bounded overlap, KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE already covers the same higher-order upper rate and nuisance elbow and applies to known uniform design.  This note therefore presents its \(\kappa=0\) result only as an explicitly total one-sided exact-uniform specialization using the known Lebesgue Gram matrix, deterministic rank rounding, singular-value flooring, clipping, and an all-dataset fallback.  That specialization gives \(R_n\leq C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\}\), with \(D_\star=1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta))\), and matches the supplied-propensity lower bound when \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), including equality without a logarithm.  Below that elbow only the exact-uniform nuisance converse remains open; for \(\kappa>0\), the higher-order frontier and critical logarithms remain open.

project_justification.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE already proves the same bounded-overlap higher-order upper rate and nuisance elbow and its theorem applies when the design is known uniform, so neither that rate nor that elbow is a novelty claim here.  Its displayed perforated-support lower witness is not a member of the singleton exact-uniform class and therefore does not settle the below-elbow nuisance converse.  No cited result supplies the sharp multivariate Bernoulli CATE benchmark at the local propensity zero for every \(\kappa\), and no cited result supplies the complete unknown-propensity higher-order frontier for \(\kappa>0\).
project_justification.niche: The distinct theorem-level content is the sharp supplied-propensity local-zero benchmark for every \(\kappa\), proved with an annular estimator and genuine full-support exact-uniform Bernoulli laws.  On the bounded-overlap slice, exact uniformity makes the Lebesgue projection Gram matrix known and permits the published higher-order architecture to be presented as a fully finite, one-sided, explicitly total implementation on every dataset.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives an explicit total annular supplied-propensity estimator and a matching exact-class Bernoulli two-point construction, proving \(R_n^e\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\) for every \(\kappa\geq0\).  It also gives the all-\(\kappa\) total first-order bracket.  For \(\kappa=0\), it specializes the already-covered KBRW higher-order rate architecture using the exact Lebesgue Gram matrix, deterministic rank rounding, singular-value flooring, clipping, and an all-dataset fallback, obtaining \(R_n\leq C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\}\).  This improves this note's first-order upper bound and, with the supplied-propensity lower bound, proves oracle-rate equality from the elbow onward; it is not presented as a new bounded-overlap rate or elbow.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, Theorems 1--2 and Definition 2 with equation (14), supplies the closest bounded-overlap pointwise CATE frontier.  Its upper theorem already has the same higher-order rate and nuisance elbow stated here and applies when the design is known uniform.  Accordingly, the present result at kappa zero is only an explicitly total one-sided exact-uniform implementation and specialization: the known Lebesgue Gram matrix, deterministic projection-rank rounding, singular-value flooring, clipping, and an all-dataset fallback make every step finite and defined on every sample.  The comparator's displayed perforated-support lower witness is outside the singleton exact-uniform class, so it does not establish the below-elbow lower bound here.  The distinct theorem-level advance is instead the all-\(\kappa\) sharp supplied-propensity local-zero result, including its full-support exact-uniform Bernoulli construction.  Kennedy2023DRCATE supplies bounded-overlap local-polynomial R-learner motivation, while LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF and ShenGaoWittenHan2020 motivate higher-order projection corrections.  RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009, Theorem 2.1, requires partition-local perturbations and does not directly cover the overlapping smooth frames needed to preserve full support.  GaoHan2020 concerns integrated random-design contrast risk; Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesign concerns scalar pointwise regression under a design zero; Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics concerns weak-overlap average-effect inference and scalar regression; and Kim2026RKHSPointwiseCATE retains a global overlap lower bound.  AtheyWager2021PolicyLearning studies downstream policy-welfare optimization under a different loss and is not used for the pointwise CATE-rate claims.  WagerAthey2018CausalForests and GRFReference motivate the application: the official \(\texttt{grf}\) workflow learns nuisance regressions and uses treatment-balance restrictions, but no claim is made that its causal forest attains the rates proved here.
body.interpretation: The all-\(\kappa\) supplied-propensity theorem quantifies the information loss caused by treatment scarcity at the corner before charging for learning the propensity multiplier.  At bounded overlap, the exact-uniform totalized specialization of the published higher-order architecture shows that unknown propensity variation does not change the pointwise CATE rate once \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\); this is an implementation and class-specialization statement, not a claim that the rate or elbow is new.  Below that elbow, the constructed estimator gives the displayed exact-uniform upper rate, but the missing lower experiment prevents declaring a nuisance penalty.  Near an actual propensity zero \(\kappa>0\), the data-only result remains the first-order bracket, so the theorem is a precision benchmark rather than an attainment claim about an existing causal forest.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The bounded-overlap higher-order upper calculation and its total exact-uniform implementation are closed, but the rate and elbow themselves are already covered by KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE.  The below-elbow exact-uniform converse remains structurally unresolved: with \(S=\alpha+\beta<\gamma\), disjoint partition-local contrast bumps at amplitude \(\delta=\ell^S\) have smoothness scale \(\delta\ell^{-\gamma}=\ell^{S-\gamma}\), overlapping smooth squared frames violate the partition-local premise of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009 and generate shared-sign multi-observation terms, and filling transition holes contributes \(nh^d\delta^2\) at the proposed scale.  For \(\kappa>0\), an upper proof must additionally control rare-treatment projection and stabilization terms, while lower constructions must repair noninteger corner powers and max-norm tie surfaces without deleting support.  No product-mixture converse is asserted.
body.honest_scope: The sharp supplied-propensity result \(R_n^e\asymp n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d+\kappa)}\) holds for every \(\kappa\geq0\) and is attained by the explicit total annular estimator.  For \(\kappa=0\), KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE already covers the same higher-order upper rate and nuisance elbow and applies to known uniform design; this paper supplies only an explicitly total one-sided exact-uniform specialization.  That specialization proves \(c n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\leq R_n\leq C\max\{n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)},n^{-1/D_\star}\}\) and hence the supplied-propensity rate when \(\alpha+\beta\geq d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), with no logarithmic multiplier at equality.  When \(\alpha+\beta<d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), no matching exact-uniform nuisance lower bound is claimed.  For \(\kappa>0\), only the established first-order data-only bracket is claimed; the higher-order upper and lower frontier, critical logarithms, and complete oracle-penalty classification remain open.  No claim is made that the existing \(\texttt{grf}\) causal forest attains any displayed rate.
